competency_fulfillment.rationale: The taking-away language the competency explicitly names is used consistently and the models are pictorial, but distractor quality undermines the task: the item beginning 'There are 20 erasers. Taking away 12 erasers leaves how many erasers?' offers 32 as a choice, a number larger than the starting quantity, and a sixteen-item picture item offers 24. A pupil who knows only that taking away makes fewer can eliminate without subtracting.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The sample covers taking away a small part, taking away most of the set, and taking away everything to leave zero, so the boundary behaviours of removal are all exercised.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The reasoning level is right, but the language is not always fit for a six-year-old reader: one true-or-false stem asserts that a removal 'leaves 1 blocks', an agreement error printed directly to a child who is still decoding the sentence.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Emoji arrays that can be counted one by one sit alongside abstract statements, a peer-error check, and choice items, which delivers the concrete-and-pictorial variety the competency asks for.

competency_alignment.rationale: Difficulty grows through the size of the collection and how much of it is removed, both of which sit inside this competency rather than beside it.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Every collection is twenty or fewer and no remainder goes negative, so the up-to-20 bound is respected in the stems.
